sources.entry: Keyboard Cowboy - The missing keyboard shortcut utility for macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/zenangst/KeyboardCowboy)

summary.one_liner: Keyboard Cowboy is a macOS keyboard shortcut and automation app that triggers workflows from shortcuts, function keys, or application events.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Keyboard Cowboy 3 as a macOS productivity app for automating repetitive actions, launching applications and scripts, controlling system settings, and manipulating files and folders from the keyboard. Workflows are organized into groups and can run sequentially or concurrently. Triggers include keyboard shortcuts, a leader key, passthrough, hold-for-X-seconds, and contextual application triggers (app opened, closed, or switched to). Commands listed in the wiki index include application, menu bar, URL, open, shortcut, script, type, macro, system, window navigation, and window tiling commands. The README states it is disabled when a password field or secure input mode is active, and that it stores data locally without sending it to third parties.
use_cases: automate repetitive Mac tasks with keyboard shortcuts
launch apps and scripts from a hotkey
trigger actions when an application opens or closes
tile and navigate windows from the keyboard
bind frequently used commands to the function key
how_to_run: Create a .env file in the repository root with APP_NAME, APP_SCHEME, APP_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER, TEAM_ID, and PACKAGE_DEVELOPMENT
notable: Contextual application triggers that run workflows when apps open, close, or gain focus
Leader key and passthrough trigger options
Window tiling and window navigation commands
Disables itself in password fields and secure input mode, per the README
Stores data locally with no collection stated in the README
caveats: Building from source needs tuist installed and a local .env file with a Team ID
README is largely marketing copy and does not document installation of the packaged app
